agentic.simpleMeaning: able to take actions toward a goal
agentic.contextMeaning: AI systems that plan, monitor, and perform tasks instead of only answering questions

orchestration.contextMeaning: managing models, tools, subagents, data, and user approvals across a workflow

multimodal.simpleMeaning: using more than one input type
multimodal.contextMeaning: combining text, images, files, video, audio, and browser context in one task

provenance.contextMeaning: evidence of where media came from and whether it was created or changed by AI

chatbot.contextMeaning: an older interface pattern that Google is moving beyond with agents and product-level AI

eyewear.contextMeaning: Android XR glasses that could put Gemini into a voice-first, physical-world interface

generative media.contextMeaning: media made or edited by tools such as Gemini Omni, Flow, Shorts Remix, or Google Pics

persistent agent.contextMeaning: a system that monitors or progresses a task even after the user closes a device

delegated attention.contextMeaning: asking an AI agent to monitor changing information and notify you when it matters

high-stakes action.contextMeaning: sending money, emails, bookings, or decisions that should require confirmation

ambient interface.contextMeaning: AI available through glasses, voice, devices, and background systems rather than one app

content credentials.contextMeaning: metadata that records how an image or video was captured, edited, or generated

synthesized update.contextMeaning: a concise report built from many sources or changing signals

fallback.contextMeaning: a safer route or model used when the first one fails or is unsuitable

latency.contextMeaning: how fast a model or system responds during interactive tasks

guardrail.contextMeaning: a boundary that limits risky AI behavior, especially around privacy or irreversible actions

audit.contextMeaning: checking what an AI system saw, decided, changed, or recommended
